title: How Nonprofit Hospitals Put Profits Over Patients

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日新闻简报 DealBook 的商业和政策记者。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔韦尔尼西，这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, non-profit hospitals were founded to help the poor.
sentences.zh: 今天的主题是，非营利医院最初是为了帮助穷人而创立的。

sentences.en: But a Times investigation has found that many are abandoning those patients in pursuit of profits.
sentences.zh: 但《时报》的一项调查发现，许多医院为了追求利润，正在抛弃这些患者。

sentences.en: My colleague,
sentences.zh: 我的同事，

sentences.en: Jessica Silver-Greenberg, on what that investigation found.
sentences.zh: 杰西卡·西尔弗-格林伯格，将为我们讲述该调查的发现。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 25th.
sentences.zh: 今天是1月25日，星期三。

sentences.en: So Jessica, tell me about this reporting you've been doing on hospitals and this patient you met,
sentences.zh: 杰西卡，跟我聊聊你关于医院以及你遇到的这位患者的报道吧，

sentences.en: Alexandra Knifors.
sentences.zh: 亚历山德拉·克尼福尔斯。
zh_words: 亚历山德拉·克尼福尔斯

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Alexandra Knifors is a woman in her 60s, and she lives in Everett,
sentences.zh: 亚历山德拉·克尼福尔斯是一位60多岁的女性，住在华盛顿州埃弗雷特，
zh_words: 亚历山德拉·克尼福尔斯

sentences.en: Washington, which is about 30 miles away from Seattle.
sentences.zh: 距离西雅图大约30英里。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: Hi, Alexandra.
sentences.zh: 嗨，亚历山德拉。

sentences.en: Hi there.
sentences.zh: 你好呀。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: I spent a fair amount of time talking to her over the course of many months last year because she had this truly harrowing medical emergency.
sentences.zh: 去年，我花了相当多的时间在几个月里与她交谈，因为她经历了一场真正痛苦的医疗紧急情况。

sentences.en: In October of 2021, she is starting to feel pretty crummy.
sentences.zh: 在2021年10月，她开始感觉很不舒服。

sentences.en: I've had some sort of unidentifiable digestive system infection.
sentences.zh: 我得了某种无法识别的消化系统感染。

sentences.en: She was having a lot of stomach pain.
sentences.zh: 她胃部剧痛。

sentences.en: She was feeling dizzy.
sentences.zh: 她感到头晕。

sentences.en: I know I couldn't get dressed, and I couldn't stand up.
sentences.zh: 我知道我无法穿衣，也无法站立。

sentences.en: And eventually, Alexandra is getting so sick that her roommate is really worried and calls an ambulance to take her to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 最终，亚历山德拉病情加重，她的室友非常担心，叫了救护车把她送到医院。

sentences.en: And Alexandra told me that at this point, she was really out of it.
sentences.zh: 亚历山德拉告诉我，当时她整个人已经迷迷糊糊了。

sentences.en: But still, on some level, she's aware that this trip could cost her a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 但从某种程度上说，她仍然意识到这次就医可能会花掉她一大笔钱。

sentences.en: You can't go to an emergency room anymore without it being thousands of dollars.
sentences.zh: 你去急诊室不可能不花上几千美元。

sentences.en: And I knew that.
sentences.zh: 我当时就知道这一点。

sentences.en: But at that point, I just didn't care.
sentences.zh: 但在那种情况下，我已经不在乎了。

sentences.en: I was so sick.
sentences.zh: 我病得太重了。

sentences.en: This is a woman who's very used to living on a very tight income.
sentences.zh: 这是一个习惯了靠极少收入过日子的女人。

sentences.en: Her only income is Social Security disability, which is about $1,700 a month, every month.
sentences.zh: 她唯一的收入是社会保障残疾补助金，每个月大约1,700美元。

sentences.en: I have constant problems with supporting my medications.
sentences.zh: 我在支付购药费用方面遇到了持续的问题。

sentences.en: I am disabled, and I'm also diabetic.
sentences.zh: 我是残疾人，而且我还患有糖尿病。

sentences.en: And so there is a lot of expensive meds on my to-be-bought liSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我的待购药清单上有很多昂贵的药物。

sentences.en: And so when she gets to the nearby hospital, she's waiting alone and scared in the emergency department.
sentences.zh: 当她到达附近的医院时，她孤零零地、害怕地在急诊室等待着。

sentences.en: And she's eventually seen by doctors who tell her that she's in pretty bad shape.
sentences.zh: 最后医生给她做了检查，告诉她情况相当糟糕。

sentences.en: Turns out that she'd been so severely dehydrated that her kidneys had failed.
sentences.zh: 原来她严重脱水，导致肾脏衰竭。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so she's told by the emergency department staff that she's going to be admitted and is probably going to have to stay for a while.
sentences.zh: 急诊室的工作人员告诉她，她需要住院，可能得住上一段时间。

sentences.en: I was worried about my cat.
sentences.zh: 我当时担心我的猫。

sentences.en: Oh, what's your cat's name?
sentences.zh: 噢，你的猫叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Stubby.
sentences.zh: 斯塔比（Stubby）。

sentences.en: Stubby?
sentences.zh: 斯塔比？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, he's kind of stubby.
sentences.zh: 对，对，它长得矮胖矮胖的。

sentences.en: Anyway, I was very alone.
sentences.zh: 总之，我当时非常孤独。

sentences.en: And I was, of course, afraid I was dying.
sentences.zh: 当然，我也害怕自己会死掉。

sentences.en: So she's worried about her health, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，她既担心自己的健康，

sentences.en: And she's worried about how much whatever treatment she needs are going to coSt. And so she described to me that every time a nurse or a doctor or anyone
sentences.zh: 又担心她需要的治疗会花多少钱。她向我描述说，每当医院的护士、医生或任何人

sentences.en: at the hospital had to do anything.
sentences.zh: 需要做任何事情时，

sentences.en: Lots and lots of blood tests and medications and...
sentences.zh: 大量大量的血液检查、药物以及……

sentences.en: Every single procedure she got, all she's seeing are dollar signs.
sentences.zh: 她经历的每一个程序，她看到的都只是美元符号。

sentences.en: ...machine, you know, that's another grand, a grand and a half.
sentences.zh: ……你知道，那台机器又要花一千、一千五百块。

sentences.en: And I knew it was going to be a huge bill.
sentences.zh: 我知道这会是一笔巨额账单。

sentences.en: I knew it was going to be enormous.
sentences.zh: 我知道它会是个天文数字。

sentences.en: I just figured, well, I'll be paying on this for the rest of my life.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，好吧，我余生都要用来还这笔债了。

sentences.en: So Alexandra eventually gets home to stubby.
sentences.zh: 所以亚历山德拉最终回到了家，和斯塔比在一起。

sentences.en: And for a couple of weeks, she doesn't hear anything from the hospital.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几周里，她没有收到医院的任何消息。

sentences.en: At first, waiting for the bill was like waiting for the other shoe to drop.
sentences.zh: 起初，等待账单就像等待另一只靴子落地。

sentences.en: And the bill arrives.
sentences.zh: 然后账单来了。

sentences.en: And while her insurance covered the bulk of her care, there was still a sizable portion, sizable for Alexandra, at least, that was left over.
sentences.zh: 虽然她的保险报销了大部分治疗费用，但仍然剩下一大笔钱——对亚历山德拉而言至少是很大一笔。

sentences.en: It was $1,950, which, of course, I didn't have because...
sentences.zh: 那是1,950美元，我当然没有，因为……

sentences.en: So more than she's taking in for the month, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这比她一个月的收入还要多，对吧？

sentences.en: A lot.
sentences.zh: 多得多。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: More than $200 more than she takes in every month.
sentences.zh: 比她每月的总收入还要多出200多美元。

sentences.en: You know, at first, I was just overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，起初我简直不知所措。

sentences.en: Like, how am I going to pay this?
sentences.zh: 心想，我怎么付得起这个？

sentences.en: I don't have $2,000.
sentences.zh: 我没有2,000美元。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So she goes on the hospital's website to see whether there are any options for her.
sentences.zh: 于是她登录医院的网站，看看有没有适合她的选项。

sentences.en: And what she sees are two choices, pay the bill in full or enter into a payment plan.
sentences.zh: 她看到了两个选择：一次性付清账单，或者分期付款。

sentences.en: And that was $162.50 a month.
sentences.zh: 分期是每月162.50美元。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, man.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，天哪。

sentences.en: Well, it means no groceries, but, you know, I can pay $162.50 a month.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这意味着买不起杂货了，不过，你知道的，我还能付得起每月162.50美元。

sentences.en: So I've made the first payment.
sentences.zh: 于是我付了第一笔。

sentences.en: And so she starts buying fewer groceries.
sentences.zh: 因此她开始减少购买杂货。

sentences.en: You know, she's going without heat.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她甚至停了暖气。

sentences.en: She starts rationing her medications, skipping days, splitting her medication in two to make it last longer.
sentences.zh: 她开始定量配给药物，跳过某些日子不吃，把药掰成两半吃以延长使用时间。

sentences.en: These are all huge sacrifices for her, all in the service of paying this bill.
sentences.zh: 为了支付这笔账单，对她来说这些都是巨大的牺牲。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And did she consider not paying it?
sentences.zh: 那她有没有考虑过不付钱？

sentences.en: It's a really good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: And something that I asked her, did you think at all about just ignoring the bill?
sentences.zh: 这也是我问过她的：你有没有想过直接无视这份账单？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: They took really good care of me.
sentences.zh: 他们把我照顾得很好。

sentences.en: And I was alive.
sentences.zh: 而且我活下来了。

sentences.en: She said whatever it takes, she is going to make good on this bill.
sentences.zh: 她说无论付出什么代价，她都要把这笔账单还清。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: In return for the care.
sentences.zh: 就为了回报这份护理。

sentences.en: OK, so this bill effectively is the catastrophe that Alexandra was worried about.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这张账单实际上就是亚历山德拉一直担心的那场灾难。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题是这样的。

sentences.en: Alexandra should never have had to pay the bill in the first place.
sentences.zh: 亚历山德拉本根本不需要支付这笔账单。

sentences.en: Never had to pay the bill?
sentences.zh: 根本不用付账单？

sentences.en: Like how?
sentences.zh: 怎么会？

sentences.en: What does that even mean?
sentences.zh: 这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: So by law, the hospital that Alexandra went to is supposed to provide free care to Alexandra and any other patient who is a low-income patient.
sentences.zh: 根据法律，亚历山德拉去的这家医院理应向亚历山德拉以及任何其他低收入患者提供免费医疗。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: That hospital is part of a massive health system called Providence.
sentences.zh: 这家医院属于一个名为普罗维デンス（Providence）的庞大医疗系统。

sentences.en: And Providence was started about 100 years ago by a group of nuns in Washington state.
sentences.zh: 普罗维登斯大约在100年前由华盛顿州的一群修女创立。

sentences.en: And it's what is called a not-for-profit hospital.
sentences.zh: 它被称为非营利医院。

sentences.en: I see the mission as the core or the heart of our organization.
sentences.zh: 我认为使命是我们组织的核心或心脏。

sentences.en: Providence's mission statement, for example, is that the hospital should be, quote, steadfast in serving all.
sentences.zh: 例如，普罗维登斯的使命宣言是：医院应当“坚定不移地服务所有人”。

sentences.en: Especially those who are poor and vulnerable.
sentences.zh: “尤其是那些贫困和弱势群体。”

sentences.en: The thing about not-for-profit hospitals is that they have this special deal with the IRS.
sentences.zh: 关于非营利医院，关键在于它们与美国国税局（IRS）有这样一项特殊协议。

sentences.en: So the IRS gives them very generous tax breaks.
sentences.zh: 国税局给予它们非常丰厚的税收减免。

sentences.en: And in return, these hospitals are supposed to do a number of things to benefit their communities, which can include giving free care to people who can't pay.
sentences.zh: 作为回报，这些医院理应为社区做一些实事，其中可以包括向付不起钱的人提供免费医疗。

sentences.en: People just like Alexandra.
sentences.zh: 就像亚历山德拉这样的人。

sentences.en: And what kind of tax breaks are we talking about when it comes to Providence?
sentences.zh: 说到普罗维登斯，我们指的是哪种税收减免？

sentences.en: Like how big?
sentences.zh: 规模有多大？

sentences.en: Very big.
sentences.zh: 非常大。

sentences.en: So in the case of Providence, about a billion dollars in tax breaks every year.
sentences.zh: 以普罗维登斯为例，他们每年获得的税收减免约为10亿美元。

sentences.en: So a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 所以是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: It's a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 这是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And their revenues, Providence's revenues, are $27 billion a year.
sentences.zh: 他们的收入，即普罗维登斯的收入，每年高达270亿美元。

sentences.en: The CEO in 2020 made $10 million.
sentences.zh: 2020年，其首席执行官的收入为1000万美元。

sentences.en: And that's not all.
sentences.zh: 这还不是全部。

sentences.en: You know, the chain is also sitting on $10 billion of cash, which it invests Wall Street style alongside private equity firms and other, you know, big deal investors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，该医疗连锁机构还坐拥100亿美元的现金，它们像华尔街那样，与私募股权公司和其他大型投资者一起进行投资。

sentences.en: But Jess, this just doesn't sound like a non-profit at all, right?
sentences.zh: 但是杰西卡，这听起来一点也不像非营利组织，对吧？

sentences.en: Wall Street, cash, war chess.
sentences.zh: 华尔街、现金、战争基金（财力雄厚）。

sentences.en: Like, what is this?
sentences.zh: 这到底算什么？

sentences.en: I mean, you're right.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你说的对。

sentences.en: It's pretty wild.
sentences.zh: 这真是太离谱了。

sentences.en: Like, welcome to the world of non-profit hospitals.
sentences.zh: 就像是，欢迎来到非营利医院的世界。

sentences.en: So my colleagues Katie Thomas, Sarah
sentences.zh: 所以我的同事凯蒂·托马斯、莎拉·

sentences.en: Cliff, and Rebecca Robbins and I spent basically a year looking into them.
sentences.zh: 克利夫、丽贝卡·罗宾斯和我基本上花了一年时间来调查它们。

sentences.en: There are 5,000 of them all over America.
sentences.zh: 全美各地共有5,000家这样的医院。

sentences.en: They make up about half the hospitals in the country.
sentences.zh: 它们占了全美大约一半的医院。

sentences.en: And they're unlike any other non-profits I've looked at.
sentences.zh: 它们与我研究过的任何其他非营利组织都不同。

sentences.en: They have the kind of cash that you might expect a company like
sentences.zh: 它们拥有的现金储备，你可能只会期待像

sentences.en: Walmart or Target or another massive for-profit operation to have.
sentences.zh: 沃尔玛、塔吉特或其他大型营利性企业才拥有。

sentences.en: And I think, Sabrina, your question about them seeming more like for-profit companies than non-profit is a good one.
sentences.zh: 萨布丽娜，我认为你提出的关于它们看起来更像是营利性公司而非非营利组织的问题问得很好。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: Providence, for example, does run itself like a for-profit business in many ways.
sentences.zh: 以普罗维登斯为例，它在许多方面确实像营利性企业一样在运作。

sentences.en: So the program that
sentences.zh: 因此，

sentences.en: Alexandra got caught up in was specifically designed to maximize the amount of money the hospital system was bringing in from some of its poorest patients.
sentences.zh: 亚历山德拉卷入的这个项目，正是专门为了最大化该医院系统从部分最贫困患者身上榨取资金而设计的。

sentences.en: So tell me about that program.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我讲讲那个项目吧。

sentences.en: So the program starts around 2018.
sentences.zh: 这个项目始于2018年前后。

sentences.en: And at the time, executives at Providence were looking for ways to save money.
sentences.zh: 当时，普罗维登斯的高管们正在寻找省钱的方法。

sentences.en: The hospital system had recently merged with another non-profit hospital.
sentences.zh: 这家医院系统最近与另一家非营利医院进行了合并。

sentences.en: And integrating these two massive systems was proving expensive.
sentences.zh: 而整合这两个庞大的系统被证明成本高昂。

sentences.en: And Providence was also spending hundreds of millions of dollars every year providing free care.
sentences.zh: 普罗维登斯每年还花费数亿美元提供免费医疗护理。

sentences.en: So they hired McKinsey & Company, the consulting firm, to come up with a plan to get patients to fork over money.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们聘请了咨询公司麦肯锡，来制定一个让患者掏钱的计划。

sentences.en: And they called it Rev Up, as in revenue up.
sentences.zh: 他们将这个计划命名为 Rev Up，寓意收入上升。

sentences.en: Oh boy.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: The centerpiece of this program were a series of scripts, like theatrical scripts, that outlined in this play exactly how employees should try to get money from patients,
sentences.zh: 这个项目的核心是一系列剧本，就像戏剧剧本一样，在这个剧本中详细规划了员工应如何设法从患者那里弄到钱，

sentences.en: even those who were supposed to receive free care.
sentences.zh: 甚至是从那些本应接受免费医疗的人身上。

sentences.en: And these documents were distributed to anyone at the hospital who might interact with patients and talk to them about payment.
sentences.zh: 这些文件分发给了医院里任何可能与患者接触并向他们谈及付款事宜的人。

sentences.en: So in one training document, for example, the employees were told, do not accept the first no.
sentences.zh: 因此，在一份培训文件中，例如，员工被告知，不要接受第一次拒绝。

sentences.en: And then staff are led through a series of questions to ask patients.
sentences.zh: 然后，员工会按照一系列问题引导患者回答。

sentences.en: The first was, how would you like to pay that today?
sentences.zh: 第一个问题是：您今天想怎么支付这笔费用？

sentences.en: If that question didn't work, employees were told to ask for half the balance.
sentences.zh: 如果这个问题没用，员工被告知要求支付一半的余额。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: If that didn't work,
sentences.zh: 如果那不管用，

sentences.en: staff could offer to set up a payment plan like the kind that Alexandra went on.
sentences.zh: 员工可以提议建立一个分期付款计划，就像亚历山大参加的那种。

sentences.en: And what's critically missing from this collection program is any way of screening patients to determine whether they should qualify for free care.
sentences.zh: 而这个催收项目最严重缺失的是任何筛选患者以确定他们是否有资格享受免费医疗的方法。

sentences.en: So they don't even know if the person they're talking to would qualify for free care.
sentences.zh: 所以他们甚至不知道与他们交谈的人是否有资格享受免费医疗。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that is quite a hard sell of give me your credit card basically.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是一场相当艰难的推销，也就是把你的信用卡交出来。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there were things that weren't included in those training scripts that also contributed to what became really a boiler room kind of atmosphere within some of Providence's
sentences.zh: 并且，那些培训剧本中未包含的内容也促成了普罗维登斯部分医院内部实际上变成了犹如高压销售室般的氛围。

sentences.en: hospitals.
sentences.zh: 医院。

sentences.en: It became so kind of built in to the culture at Providence that on one Halloween at one of Providence's hospitals, an employee dressed up as a wrestler named Rev Up Ricky.
sentences.zh: 这种氛围深深融入了普罗维登斯的文化中，以至于在普罗维登斯某家医院的一个万圣节，一名员工打扮成了一个名叫“Rev Up 里奇”的摔跤手。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And another costume during this Halloween featured a giant cardboard dollar sign that had
sentences.zh: 在这个万圣节的另一个造型中，出现了一个巨大的纸板美元符号，上面印着

sentences.en: how printed on it, which was a reference to the way that staff were supposed to ask patients how not whether they would like to pay.
sentences.zh: “如何”这个词，这是指员工应该如何询问患者如何付款，而不是是否愿意付款。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: And how did employees feel about this?
sentences.zh: 员工对这件事有什么感受？

sentences.en: I mean, this is a very potentially deeply uncomfortable thing to ask patients.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，向患者提出要求是一件非常具有潜在深度不适感的事情。

sentences.en: A lot of the employees that I spoke to, some of whom had no more money than the patients they were hounding, were really unsettled by this.
sentences.zh: 我交谈过的许多员工，其中有些人并不比他们催逼的患者更有钱，对此感到非常不安。

sentences.en: Because they were also aware of just how rich this hospital system is.
sentences.zh: 因为他们同样清楚这家医院系统有多么富有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so one woman who worked in the emergency department said that really the tactics that she was told to use struck her as completely predatory.
sentences.zh: 因此，一位在急诊室工作的女士说，她被告知要使用的策略确实让她觉得完全具有掠夺性。

sentences.en: She was told to approach patients almost as soon as doctors had finished examining them.
sentences.zh: 她被要求几乎在医生刚完成检查后就去接近患者。

sentences.en: So like doctor leaves the room and she walks in and she crouches at their bedside and asks for money.
sentences.zh: 就像医生离开房间，她走进去，蹲在他们的床头要求付款。

sentences.en: And she was required to put in patients' medical charts that she had repeatedly asked for payments.
sentences.zh: 并且她被要求在患者的病历中记下她曾多次催收费用。

sentences.en: Because if that wasn't in there and her bosses caught wind of it, she would suffer the consequences.
sentences.zh: 因为如果没有记录在案且被她的老板发现，她将承担后果。

sentences.en: She would be called out.
sentences.zh: 她会被公开批评。

sentences.en: And it was in their medical charts?
sentences.zh: 这被写进他们的病历里了？

sentences.en: That's crazy.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: It was written into their medical charts.
sentences.zh: 它确实被写进了他们的病历里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's particularly jarring, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这特别刺耳，对吧？

sentences.en: Because of the origin and mission of Providence, helping poor people, providing care for poor people.
sentences.zh: 因为普罗维登斯的起源和使命是帮助穷人，为穷人提供医疗护理。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what do executives at Providence say about RevUp and the company culture?
sentences.zh: 那么普罗维登斯的高管对 RevUp 和公司文化是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Like, how do they explain this?
sentences.zh: 比如说，他们是怎么解释这一点的？

sentences.en: Well, we were able to get on the phone with Providence's chief financial officer who did say that our findings were concerning.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们得以电话采访了普罗维登斯的首席财务官，他确实表示我们的调查结果令人担忧。

sentences.en: And he emphasized that the hospital system wants to get it right, to do well by their patients.
sentences.zh: 并且他强调，该医院系统希望把事情做好，真正为患者服务好。

sentences.en: But Providence also pretty emphatically defended its practices.
sentences.zh: 但普罗维登斯同时也相当强硬地为其做法进行了辩护。

sentences.en: And they pointed out to us that in Washington state, for example,
sentences.zh: 他们向我们指出，例如在华盛顿州，

sentences.en: Providence provides more free health care than any other hospital.
sentences.zh: 普罗维登斯提供的免费医疗比任何其他医院都要多。

sentences.en: But the thing is, Providence was just one of the hospital systems we looked into that had strayed far from its charitable roots and was acting more like a for-profit company.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，普罗维登斯只是我们调查的偏离其慈善根基、表现得更像营利性公司的其中一个医院系统。

sentences.en: And sometimes that kind of behavior had really serious consequences for the health of patients.
sentences.zh: 有时这种行为对患者的健康产生了非常严重的后果。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能获取所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你尚未订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《时报》应用程序，并获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Jessica, you said that Providence was just one example of the for-profit behavior you found while investigating not-for-profit hospitals.
sentences.zh: 那么杰西卡，你刚才说普罗维登斯只是你在调查非营利医院时发现的营利性行为的一个例子。

sentences.en: What else did you find in your reporting?
sentences.zh: 你在报道中还发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, one of the most shocking examples of this kind of rapacious for-profit behavior came from another giant not-for-profit health system called Bon Secours.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这种贪婪的营利性行为最令人震惊的例子之一来自另一个名为博内塞库尔的庞大非营利医疗系统。

sentences.en: And Bon Secours found a way to just mint hundreds of millions of dollars off a tiny poor hospital in Virginia called Richmond Community.
sentences.zh: 博内塞库尔找到了一种方法，从弗吉尼亚州一家名为里奇蒙社区医院的小型贫困医院身上赚取了数亿美元。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: How did they do that?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: Well, first, let me tell you a little bit about Richmond Community.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，让我向你介绍一点关于里奇蒙社区医院的情况。

sentences.en: It was founded in the 1900s by Black doctors who weren't allowed to work at the white hospitals across town.
sentences.zh: 它由黑人医生于 20 世纪创立，当时他们不被允许在镇上的白人医院工作。

sentences.en: And it was a modest building ringed by public housing projects.
sentences.zh: 这是一座简朴的建筑，周围环绕着公共住宅区。

sentences.en: And it didn't have all the services at larger hospitals, but it did have specialists in cancer, heart, and lung disease.
sentences.zh: 它没有大型医院的所有服务，但它拥有癌症、心脏和肺病方面的专家。

sentences.en: And people were proud of this little hospital that could.
sentences.zh: 人们为这家充满进取精神的小医院感到自豪。

sentences.en: It was a place where Black patients could be treated by Black doctors, and there was a sense of pride both in its history and its mission.
sentences.zh: 这是一个黑人患者可以由黑人医生治疗的地方，人们对它的历史和使命都有一种自豪感。

sentences.en: But over the years, for a bunch of reasons, it got harder and harder for independent institutions like Community to stay afloat.
sentences.zh: 但多年来，由于种种原因，像社区医院这样的独立机构维持运营变得越来越困难。

sentences.en: So, fast forward to 1995, the doctors who owned it sold it to Bon Secours.
sentences.zh: 所以，快进到 1995 年，拥有它的医生把它卖给了博内塞库尔。

sentences.en: And executives at Bon Secours eventually realized they could use this poor hospital to tap into a very lucrative federal drug program.
sentences.zh: 博内塞库尔的高管们最终意识到，他们可以利用这家贫困医院来接入一个非常 lucrative（利润丰厚）的联邦药物项目。

sentences.en: The program allows hospitals like Community, that serve low-income patients, to buy prescription drugs at steep, steep discounts, and then charge insurers full price
sentences.zh: 该项目允许像社区医院这样服务于低收入患者的医院以极大的折扣购买处方药，然后向保险公司收取全价

sentences.en: for those same drugs and pocket the difference.
sentences.zh: 购买这些相同的药物，并把差价放入囊中。

sentences.en: So, seems reasonable.
sentences.zh: 所以，这看起来很合理。

sentences.en: Poor neighborhoods should have discounts on drugs.
sentences.zh: 贫困社区应该享有药品折扣。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: That was the intention of the program, which is called 340B.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个名为 340B 的项目的初衷。

sentences.en: The theory behind this program was that non-profit hospitals would invest the savings, that windfall, into their communities.
sentences.zh: 该项目背后的理论是非营利医院会将节省下来的资金，即这笔意外之财，投入到他们的社区中。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But after Bon Secours bought Richmond Community, it figured out how to use this program to supercharge its profits.
sentences.zh: 但在博内塞库尔收购里奇蒙社区医院后，它摸索出了如何利用这个项目来极大地增加其利润。

sentences.en: What Bon Secours did is they began building clinics in wealthier neighborhoods where patients had private insurance.
sentences.zh: 博内塞库尔的做法是，他们开始在富裕社区建设诊所，那里的患者拥有私人保险。

sentences.en: And each of these new locations, even though they were far away from
sentences.zh: 尽管这些新的医疗点距离

sentences.en: Richmond Community and not serving poor patients, were still allowed to take advantage of the same drug discounts.
sentences.zh: 里奇蒙社区医院很远，也没有为贫困患者服务，但它们仍然被允许利用相同的药品折扣。

sentences.en: So, Bon Secours just basically franchises this program to a whole bunch of different locations, even though those communities weren't meant to receive the discount.
sentences.zh: 因此，博内塞库尔基本上将这个项目特许经营到了许多不同的地方，尽管这些社区本来并不属于享受折扣的对象。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And on paper, these new locations were just extensions of Richmond
sentences.zh: 在纸面上，这些新的医疗点只是里奇蒙

sentences.en: Community Hospital.
sentences.zh: 社区医院的延伸。

sentences.en: So, how much money does that make Bon Secours?
sentences.zh: 那么这给博内塞库尔带来了多少钱？

sentences.en: And where does it go?
sentences.zh: 这些钱都去哪儿了？

sentences.en: So, we know that Richmond Community Hospital generated about $100 million a year through this program.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们知道里奇蒙社区医院通过这个项目每年产生大约 1 亿美元的收入。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: A lot.
sentences.zh: 很多。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: A lot.
sentences.zh: 很多。

sentences.en: The vast majority of that revenue from our reporting is thanks to this program.
sentences.zh: 根据我们的报道，绝大部分收入都要归功于这个项目。

sentences.en: But then, to get back to your question, where did this money go?
sentences.zh: 但接着，回到你的问题，这些钱都去哪儿了？

sentences.en: I mean, that is one of the things that we started to investigate.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是我们开始调查的事情之一。

sentences.en: And that's a really big question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大的问题。

sentences.en: We know that executives at Bon Secours are paid like for-profit executives, similar to Providence.
sentences.zh: 我们知道博内塞库尔的高管们的薪酬就像营利性高管一样，类似于普罗维登斯。

sentences.en: The CEO at Bon Secours made $6 million in 2020.
sentences.zh: 博内塞库尔的首席执行官在 2020 年赚了 600 万美元。

sentences.en: And we also know from our reporting that Bon Secours' clinics in wealthy neighborhoods
sentences.zh: 从我们的报道中我们也知道，博内塞库尔在富裕社区的诊所

sentences.en: have really great amenities, marble fountains and golf carts to shuttle patients from their cars.
sentences.zh: 拥有非常棒的设施，比如大理石喷泉和用高尔夫球车接送患者往返停车场。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Bon Secours was really stripping services from Richmond Community Hospital.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，博内塞库尔却在大肆削减里奇蒙社区医院的服务。

sentences.en: In 2017, it closed the ICU.
sentences.zh: 2017 年，它关闭了重症监护室。

sentences.en: And one of the doctors we spoke to, whose family was involved in the founding of Richmond Community, said that closing the ICU really took the heart out of the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我们采访过的一位医生，其家族参与了里奇蒙社区医院的创立，他说关闭重症监护室真的抽走了医院的心脏。

sentences.en: Because once the ICU was closed, the lung specialists and other specialists like cardiologists had nowhere to treat seriously ill patients.
sentences.zh: 因为一旦重症监护室关闭，肺病专家和心脏病专家等其他专家就没有地方治疗重症患者了。

sentences.en: So you start to see this attrition, this exodus of specialists.
sentences.zh: 所以你开始看到这种损耗，看到专家的大批出走。

sentences.en: You know, the lung specialists leave and then the cardiologists follow them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，肺病专家离开了，然后心脏病专家也随之离开。

sentences.en: And Bon Secours does not replace these doctors.
sentences.zh: 而博内塞库尔并没有更换这些医生。

sentences.en: So Richmond Community really becomes a shell of itself.
sentences.zh: 因此，里奇蒙社区医院真正变成了一个空壳。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is all pretty incredible, right?
sentences.zh: 好的，所以这一切都挺令人难以置信的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, you have this larger system,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你有这样一个更大的系统，

sentences.en: Bon Secours, making more and more money off the back of this smaller hospital, Richmond Community, even as it stripped that same hospital of its services.
sentences.zh: 博内塞库尔，依靠较小的里奇蒙社区医院来赚取越来越多的钱，甚至同时剥夺了这家医院的服务。

sentences.en: So what do the doctors and the people at Richmond Community Hospital have to say about this?
sentences.zh: 那么里奇蒙社区医院的医生和员工对此有何看法？

sentences.en: Well, so one doctor we interviewed who worked in Richmond Community's emergency department until 2018 he put it pretty bluntly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们采访过的一位在里奇蒙社区医院急诊室工作到 2018 年的医生直言不讳地表达了这一点。

sentences.en: He said Bon Secours was basically laundering money through this poor hospital to its wealthy outposts.
sentences.zh: 他说，博内塞库尔基本上是通过这家贫困医院向其富裕的分支机构洗钱。

sentences.en: And he was outraged about it.
sentences.zh: 他对这种做法感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And he said it was all about profits.
sentences.zh: 并且他说这一切全是为了利润。

sentences.en: At this nonprofit hospital.
sentences.zh: 在这家非营利医院里。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And how does Bon Secours justify this?
sentences.zh: 博内塞库尔又是如何为此辩解的呢？

sentences.en: What do they say to the people inside Richmond Community Hospital who need to go to the ICU and can't?
sentences.zh: 他们对里奇蒙社区医院内部那些需要去重症监护室却去不了的人说些什么？

sentences.en: So Bon Secours' argument, both to the doctors who protested these cuts and to patients, was that if
sentences.zh: 所以博内塞库尔无论是对抗议这些削减的医生还是对患者的论点都是，如果

sentences.en: patients in the East End needed services that Richmond Community Hospital doesn't offer, they can always go to other hospitals in the Bon Secours system.
sentences.zh: 东区的患者需要里奇蒙社区医院不提供的服务，他们随时可以去博内塞库尔系统中的其他医院。

sentences.en: But there's a problem with that, which is those hospitals are miles away.
sentences.zh: 但这里有个问题，那就是这些医院在数英里之外。

sentences.en: And they're not easily reachable by public transit for the people who live near Richmond Community Hospital.
sentences.zh: 对于住在里奇蒙社区医院附近的人来说，乘坐公共交通并不容易到达那里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And a lot of those people don't have cars.
sentences.zh: 而且其中许多人没有汽车。

sentences.en: And in practice, we found cases where the fact that
sentences.zh: 在实践中，我们发现了一些案例，其中

sentences.en: Richmond Community Hospital was so diminished actually harmed patients, really harmed them.
sentences.zh: 里奇蒙社区医院的严重萎缩实际上伤害了患者，对他们造成了真正的伤害。

sentences.en: I mean, a case that has stuck with me throughout this reporting that I was really pretty haunted by was the case of a man named Norman Odie.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在整个采访过程中一直萦绕在我心头、让我感到挥之不去的案例是一个名叫诺曼·奥迪的男子的案例。

sentences.en: So this summer, he was rushed by ambulance to Richmond Community Hospital.
sentences.zh: 今年夏天，他被救护车紧急送往里奇蒙社区医院。

sentences.en: He was in his 60s and was doubled over in pain.
sentences.zh: 他60多岁，痛得直不起腰。

sentences.en: And he was babbling at this point pretty incoherently.
sentences.zh: 此时他已经语无伦次、神志不清了。

sentences.en: And blood tests suggested septic shock, which is an emergency that requires resources and the expertise of an intensive care unit to treat.
sentences.zh: 血液检测显示为感染性休克，这是一种需要重症监护室的资源和专业知识来治疗的紧急情况。

sentences.en: But Richmond, as we've said, had closed its ICU in 2017.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所说，里奇蒙医院已于 2017 年关闭了其重症监护室。

sentences.en: So there was no ICU for him to go to.
sentences.zh: 所以没有重症监护室供他入住。

sentences.en: And it took several hours for him to be transported to another hospital.
sentences.zh: 他花了几个小时才被转运到另一家医院。

sentences.en: And he deteriorated on the way there.
sentences.zh: 他在途中病情恶化。

sentences.en: And he later died of sepsis.
sentences.zh: 并且他后来死于败血症。

sentences.en: God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And two people who cared for Mr. Odie said the delay had most likely contributed to his death.
sentences.zh: 关心奥迪先生的两位人士表示，这种耽搁极大地导致了他的死亡。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That is an indictment of the decisions that the hospital system made.
sentences.zh: 这是对该医院系统所做决策的强烈谴责。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So this is the kind of human toll that we saw, where in theory, what Bon Secours is saying makes perfect sense.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们所看到的那种人类代价，按理说，邦瑟科尔斯医院的说法完全合情合理。

sentences.en: But the mechanics of it break down, as we saw.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们所看到的，它的运作机制崩溃了。

sentences.en: So Jessica, just stepping back here for a second, your reporting has shown that many nonprofit hospitals, including some of the biggest hospital systems in the country, are
sentences.zh: 杰西卡，我们退一步来看，你的报道显示，许多非营利性医院，包括该国一些最大的医院系统，

sentences.en: really effectively operating as for-profit companies.
sentences.zh: 实际上都在像营利性公司一样运作。

sentences.en: But they're still getting these huge and lucrative tax breaks and subsidies from the government.
sentences.zh: 但它们仍然从政府那里获得巨额且利润丰厚的税收减免和补贴。

sentences.en: So I guess my question for you is, how did we get here?
sentences.zh: 所以我想问你的问题是，我们是怎么走到这一步的？

sentences.en: I mean, why have nonprofit hospitals gone in this direction?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为什么非营利性医院会朝这个方向发展？

sentences.en: So when we talk to nonprofit hospital executives, they say that they're in a pretty tough spot.
sentences.zh: 当我们与非营利性医院的高管交谈时，他们说自己处境相当艰难。

sentences.en: They're competing, you know, with a whole host of rivals, not just other not-for-profit hospitals, but also for-profit hospitals.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们要与众多的竞争对手竞争，不仅有其他非营利性医院，还有营利性医院。

sentences.en: And in order to compete and live up to their mission, they need to be strong financial stewards.
sentences.zh: 为了竞争并履行他们的使命，他们需要成为强有力的财务管理者。

sentences.en: The phrase that we heard again and again when we spoke to executives is the phrase, no margin, no mission.
sentences.zh: 我们在与高管交谈时反复听到的一句话是：没有利润就没有使命。

sentences.en: The idea is that if you're not in a strong financial position, if you don't have a lot of cash, you won't survive and you won't be able to
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，如果你没有强健的财务状况，如果你没有大量现金，你就无法生存，如果你不复存在，你也将无法

sentences.en: fulfill your mission if you don't exist, right?
sentences.zh: 履行你的使命，对吧？

sentences.en: So executives justify this kind of profit-seeking behavior because they say, look, we want to expand.
sentences.zh: 因此，高管们为这种追求利润的行为辩护，因为他们说，你看，我们要扩张。

sentences.en: We want to provide more care for more people.
sentences.zh: 我们希望为更多人提供更多的护理。

sentences.en: And in order to do that, we're competing for investors.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，我们正在竞逐投资者。

sentences.en: We're trying to make sure that we can borrow money at low interest rates so that we can expand less expensively.
sentences.zh: 我们正试图确保我们能够以低利率借到资金，以便我们能以较低的成本进行扩张。

sentences.en: But as your reporting has shown us, there are real consequences to that behavior.
sentences.zh: 但正如你的报道向我们展示的那样，这种行为带来了真正的后果。

sentences.en: We found that much of the problem lies with the IRS.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，很大一部分问题在于国税局（IRS）。

sentences.en: So the IRS is not really policing these hospitals to see whether or not they are following the rules.
sentences.zh: 因此，国税局并没有真正在监管这些医院，以查看它们是否在遵守规则。

sentences.en: And the problem is that the rules themselves that hospitals have to follow to justify their tax exemptions are pretty squishy.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，医院为了证明其税收豁免合理性而必须遵守的规则本身就相当模糊。

sentences.en: So the IRS now allows hospitals to provide a broad range of very loosely defined benefits to justify their tax breaks.
sentences.zh: 因此，国税局现在允许医院提供广泛的、定义非常宽松的福利，来证明其税收减免的合理性。

sentences.en: And some hospitals have seized upon this new leeway and argued that things like employees' salaries counted towards the IRS requirement
sentences.zh: 一些医院抓住了这种新的余地，辩称诸如员工薪水之类的支出可以计入国税局的要求，

sentences.en: or building a shiny new surgical center in a suburb where all the patients are pretty wealthy.
sentences.zh: 或者在所有患者都相当富裕的郊区建立一个崭新的外科中心。

sentences.en: That also counts towards fulfilling this, again, pretty squishy, loosely defined community benefit.
sentences.zh: 这也算作履行了这种同样是非常模糊、定义宽松的社区福利。

sentences.en: Jess, is any of what these hospitals were doing illegal?
sentences.zh: 杰西，这些医院所做的事情有非法的吗？

sentences.en: For the most part, no.
sentences.zh: 大部分没有。

sentences.en: With Providence, the attorney general in Washington state actually sued the hospital system in February of last year and did argue that Providence's collection practices
sentences.zh: 以普罗维登斯医院为例，华盛顿州的州总检察长实际上在去年二月起诉了该医院系统，并辩称普罗维登斯的催收做法

sentences.en: were in violation of the state law, in part because they were using debt collectors to pursue, and the scale of this is pretty stunning, about 55,000 patient accounts
sentences.zh: 违反了州法律，部分原因是因为他们使用收债公司来追讨——这个规模相当惊人——大约55000名患者的账户，

sentences.en: that the state attorney general argued should never have been sent to collections.
sentences.zh: 州总检察长认为这些账户本就不应该被送交收债公司。

sentences.en: And the lawsuit said that Providence wrongly claimed that those patients owed more than $73 million.
sentences.zh: 诉讼称，普罗维登斯错误地声称这些患者欠款超过7300万美元。

sentences.en: But Providence fervently denies that anything they did was illegal.
sentences.zh: 但普罗维登斯强烈否认他们的任何行为是非法的。

sentences.en: So that's the closest that we came to kind of allegations of illegal behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们最接近非法行为指控的一次。

sentences.en: And Jess, do we have a sense of what the decision might be in that lawsuit?
sentences.zh: 杰西，我们大概知道这起诉讼的判决可能会是什么吗？

sentences.en: We don't.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: We have some clues as to how it might go, although I could never predict how a lawsuit of any kind is going to go.
sentences.zh: 我们有一些关于它可能会如何发展的线索，尽管我永远无法预测任何类型的诉讼会如何发展。

sentences.en: But Providence has already said it will stop using debt collectors to pursue money from low-income patients who should qualify for free care in Washington state.
sentences.zh: 但普罗维登斯已经表示，它将停止使用收债公司向华盛顿州本应有资格获得免费护理的低收入患者追讨资金。

sentences.en: So that is a move.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个举措。

sentences.en: And actually, shortly after our story on Providence ran, the hospital system said it would refund payments that more than 700 low-income patients made.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我们关于普罗维登斯的报道播出的不久后，该医院系统表示将退还700多名低收入患者支付的款项。

sentences.en: And they said that those people had been wrongly charged for medical care that should have been free.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，这些人被错误地收取了本应免费的医疗费用。

sentences.en: And what about Alexandra?
sentences.zh: 那亚历山德拉呢？

sentences.en: Did she get her money back?
sentences.zh: 她拿回她的钱了吗？

sentences.en: Well, so Alexandra's story has a happy-ish ending.
sentences.zh: 嗯，亚历山德拉的故事算是一个比较圆满的结局。

sentences.en: She does get her money back.
sentences.zh: 她确实拿回了她的钱。

sentences.en: But this whole ordeal with Providence has really stuck with her.
sentences.zh: 但与普罗维登斯的这整个磨难确实在她心中留下了阴影。

sentences.en: You know, when I asked her what she thinks of Providence now and how she might feel about having to go back to the hospital if she gets sick with anything else,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我问她现在对普罗维登斯有什么看法，以及如果她因为其他任何事情生病而不得不回到医院会作何感想时，

sentences.en: she said she's afraid of the hospital.
sentences.zh: 她说她害怕这家医院。

sentences.en: You know, in the part of Washington state where she lives,
sentences.zh: 你知道，在华盛顿州她居住的那片区域，

sentences.en: Providence is really the only game in town.
sentences.zh: 普罗维登斯真的是唯一的选择。

sentences.en: So if she does have to go back to the hospital,
sentences.zh: 所以如果她真的必须回到医院，

sentences.en: she's worried that Providence will refuse to treat her because of how vocal she has been about what happened to her.
sentences.zh: 她担心普罗维登斯会因为她公开谈论自己遭遇的事情而拒绝为她治疗。

sentences.en: And I did try to reassure her that if Providence were to deny her life-saving care, that would likely be illegal.
sentences.zh: 我确实试图让她放心，如果普罗维登斯拒绝为她提供挽救生命的护理，那很可能是非法的。

sentences.en: But honestly, I'm not sure that did much to assuage her concerns.
sentences.zh: 但老实说，我不确定这能在多大程度上减轻她的担忧。

sentences.en: Because, you know, she's still sick.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，她仍然生病。

sentences.en: And the way she sees it, this hospital system took advantage of her once.
sentences.zh: 在她看来，这个医院系统曾经利用过她一次。

sentences.en: Why wouldn't they do it again?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么不会再做一次呢？

sentences.en: Jess, thank you.
sentences.zh: 杰西，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: After the Times investigation ran,
sentences.zh: 在《泰晤士报》的调查报道发表后，

sentences.en: Richmond's mayor called for a federal investigation into Bon Secours, while the hospital system pledged to reinvest in the neighborhood around Richmond Community Hospital,
sentences.zh: 里士满市长呼吁对邦瑟科尔斯医院进行联邦调查，而该医院系统则承诺在里士满社区医院周边的社区重新投资，

sentences.en: including adding back specialties like cardiology and pulmonary care.
sentences.zh: 包括增设心脏病学和肺病学等专科。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, classified documents were found in the home of former Vice President Mike Pence,
sentences.zh: 周二，在前副总统迈克·彭斯的家中发现了机密文件，

sentences.en: raising more questions about how classified materials are handled at the top levels of government.
sentences.zh: 这引发了人们对政府最高层如何处理机密材料的更多质疑。

sentences.en: The Department of Justice is currently investigating both Donald Trump and Joe Biden for classified materials found in their homes.
sentences.zh: 司法部目前正在调查唐纳德·特朗普和乔·拜登，因为在他们的家中发现了机密材料。

sentences.en: The documents were, quote, inadvertently boxed and transported to Pence's home in Indiana at the end of the Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 这些文件在特朗普政府卸任时，据称是“无意中”被装箱并运至彭斯位于印第安纳州的家中的。

sentences.en: Aides found them and notified the National Archives.
sentences.zh: 助手们发现了这些文件并通知了国家档案馆。

sentences.en: They said Pence was unaware of their existence.
sentences.zh: 他们表示彭斯并不知道这些文件的存在。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that the Biden administration plans to send as many as 50 Abrams tanks to Ukraine, a major new step in arming Kiev at a critical phase of the war.
sentences.zh: 据《泰晤士报》报道，拜登政府计划向乌克兰派遣多达50辆艾布拉姆斯主战坦克，这是在战争的关键阶段武装基辅的又一重大新举措。

sentences.en: The administration had previously decided against sending the tanks, but reversed course, apparently in an effort to get Germany to send its tanks.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府此前曾决定不派遣这些坦克，但随后改变了立场，显然是为了促使德国派遣其主战坦克。

sentences.en: German officials privately said that they would only send their Leopard tanks if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 德国官员私下表示，只有在美方同意派遣艾布拉姆斯坦克的情况下，他们才会派遣“豹”式坦克。

sentences.en: agreed to send the AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 周二晚上，德国新闻媒体报道称，德国总理奥拉夫·朔尔茨已经决定派遣这些坦克。

sentences.en: On Tuesday night, German news outlets were reporting that German Chancellor Olaf Scholz had already decided to send them.
sentences.zh: 他将于周三在议会发表讲话。

sentences.en: He will address Parliament on Wednesday.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由阿斯塔·查塔维迪和威尔·里德制作，亚历克斯·斯特恩提供了帮助。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Asta Chattarvedi and Will Reed, with help from Alex Stern.
sentences.zh: 节目由迈克尔·贝努瓦剪辑，包含丹·鲍威尔、玛丽安·洛扎诺和罗温·内米スト的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德担任音频工程。

sentences.en: It was edited by Michael Benoit, contains original music by Dan Powell, Marian Lozano, and Rowan Nemisto, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢凯蒂·托马斯。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Katie Thomas.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由旺德利的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔维内西。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了许多自称是改革派的人士。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场痛苦、混乱有时甚至激动人心的争斗之中。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都会》节目中，由我萨拉·科尼格为您讲述人们试图保持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 《都会》。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 您可以在任何收听播客的地方收听。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
